This is a "found phone" thriller/horror game where you are going through a missing person's phone to figure out what happened to her.

The puzzles are fun, especially the ones where you have to pose as another person in chats or figure out passwords, and I liked the storyline that emerges (the happy ending almost feels like a Black Mirror episode) but the acting is only so-so and both of the primary characters you deal with are annoying.

The game does lose a little of its charm if you're not playing it on an actual phone, but as long as you don't mind cheesy FMV and a few gratuitous jump scares, you could definitely do worse.

Absolutely loved the game. There are so many Easter eggs to find and 4 different endings as well. Great horror aspect too: it's not quite a typical horror game, it's more unsettling and creepy than terrifying. It's not the game you'll be having nightmares about for the next 3 days, it's the one you'll be thinking about months from now when you're sitting in the dark.  And the begin + mode that speeds up the chat once you finish the game is awesome. Without it, I would not have had the patience to replay it for different endings. It's not super time consuming: I finished it in two and a half hours the first time, though I did watch a youtuber playthrough so I knew a bit, and once I had begin+ to speed up chat and knew what to do, it took me an hour. It doesn't have much replay value once you get all the endings and achievements, so overall, you really don't get that much playtime compared to other games, but the price reflects that. Overall, definitely a worthwhile purchase.

In Simulacra you find yourself in possession of a stranger's (Anna) phone, who seems to have come to some harm. Through interactions with her phone via video logs, old chat messages, pictures, etc, you gain access to Anna's backstory. Going forward, primarily through "live" chats with Anna's acquaintances, and interactions with some of the other apps on the phone, you unravel the story.

Pros:
[list]
[*] The story progression as implemented through the interactions with the phone apps is OK.
[*] The real-life acting done by Anna and Taylor was good.
[*] The concept of this experience was novel (at least to me).
[/list]

YMMV:
[list]
[*] There are different endings possible, as a function of your choices. I typically don't like this choose-your-adventure type of feature, as it turns into a "guess what the dev" wants me to say sort of thing. Also, this game is nowhere near interesting enough to warrant a second play through, so you are stuck with whatever ending your seemingly random choices yield. For me, this was the "bad" (maybe even super bad?) ending, which left a bad taste in my mouth, and made me feel as though I had wasted my time.
[/list]

Cons:
[list]
[*] The two oft repeated mini-games aren't really fun, and seem shoe-horned in, in an effort to somehow make this more into a game. It doesn't really work. I would classify this as an "experience" more than a "game".
[*] The story itself was underwhelming. 
[/list]

Conclusion: Read the reviews carefully before purchasing this one and get it on sale. It may be a mildly amusing way to pass several hours, but it certainly isn't for everyone. Giving a weak-thumbs up due to binary rating system.

Overall: 5.0/10

[b]SIMULACRA[/b] is detective visual novel with a hint of horror and a unique presentation and a couple of simple puzzles. The whole story unfolds on the screen of a phone lost by a missing girl. You start by looking through her videos, photos and chat history. There are even some interesting puzzles where you have to answer personal questions to restore password. But then the game shifts to the classic visual novel style, which uses chat windows instead of dialogue boxes. It becomes boring and the dialogue writing is kind of bad, expect stupid jokes and useless sentences. Another thing that made my walkthrough impossible are jumpscares, why put them in a game where you have to focus to read text? Somebody's gonna have a heart attack from this.

[b]Pros:[/b]
+ Unique presentation
+ Interesting 30-60 minutes of gameplay in the beginning

[b]Cons:[/b]
- Jumpscares
- Boring dialogue that tries too much to be funny
- Not much in terms of gameplay

This game is atmospheric and really freaky the first play through. Honestly, I don't like the ending reveal, but I think it will hit differently for other people. Even not being a fan of the reveal, I definitely DO NOT feel I wasted my time and still had fun. Some closing points:

-After playing this on PC, my opinion is that it's probably much more immersive to play on a phone.
-There are jump scares, so don't play if you don't like those.
-The game has a lot of footage and audio recordings of the "starving actor" variety, as well as incredible amounts of stock photos passed off as "real." Respect to the actors, but I think a lot of the videos, audio, and "pictures I happen to have" really pull you out of the story.

Ultimately, if you like gettin spooked, I would get this game. Its flaws are so small in comparison to the amount of enjoyment you get from it.

The story is very good and really well paced , the characters and voice acting as well are both really well done , its got a goofy feeling but also a serious tone when it needs to be serious. Overall an absolutely awesome game to experience for the first time, highly recommended,
